extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Coast Guard contract administrators, COTRs, Contracting Officers, MLCPAC staff, and senior USCG leadership overseeing A-76 commercial activity contracts
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and oversight guidance for A-76 contracted commercial activities (food service, security, housing maintenance, base industrial) focusing on cost comparisons vs a Most Efficient Organization (MEO), contractor performance, contract administration, QA, training, and causes of cost increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall contract performance assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance of this contract has been determined to be satisfactory to excellent by the Government and contractor over the life of this contract, with no deductions taken for unsatisfactory performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Government and customer assessments to rate overall performance; document any deductions for unsatisfactory performance and the basis for them. Note that early difficulties may be resolved (e.g., change of PM) and affect overall ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Manager (PM) prior-service experience and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The PM being a motivated prior service SS was a big factor in the success of a contract operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate PMs for relevant prior service experience and ability to relate to military customers; continuity of PM during contractor changeover helps smooth transitions and improve outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and availability of contract price adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Wages and food prices increased, but the contractor wasn’t afforded the opportunity to request an increase until the second option year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure procedures allow timely requests and application of economic price adjustments (including DOL wage determinations and food price adjustments) so contractors can seek relief when costs rise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor–customer relationship quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The relationship between the contractor and his customers has been very good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and document working relationships (COTR reports, customer feedback) as part of performance evaluation; good relationships can enable flexibility and informal accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: COTR training adequacy and QA paperwork clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The present COTR ... stated that the training was a good basic course in contract fundamentals, but that QA paperwork requirements were still a gray area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate COTR training for practical applicability to day-to-day duties and QA tasks; provide follow-up or tailored training to address 'gray areas' in QA paperwork and surveillance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract specification breadth and contractor flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor had been 'flexible' many times during contract performance due to the broad specifications in the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review specification scope: broad specs can allow useful flexibility (e.g., supplying food at cost for morale events) but may also hide contingencies; document when flexibility is used and whether it affects contract cost or fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and sufficiency of contract file documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: When contract administration was transferred ... it was found that the contract files were incomplete. These contract files should have been able to stand on their own for later review, however two files reviewed could not fully explain why some actions were taken and others were not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain complete contract files that independently document negotiations, obligations, modifications, and rationales so subsequent administrators can reconstruct actions; incomplete files impair oversight and audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of DOL wage determinations and economic price adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Under MLCPAC contract administration, the DOL wage determination increase was applied and combined with an economic price adjustment for food.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track and correctly apply DOL wage determinations and economic price adjustment clauses; document requests, approvals, and resulting obligation changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of MEO cost comparison and 10% personnel-cost threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: All of these contracts were initially awarded because they were lower than the Government’s MEO by 10% or greater of MEO personnel cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use OMB/COMDT MEO procedures to compute 'should cost' and apply a clear threshold (e.g., 10% personnel-cost savings) when deciding to contract out; ensure MEO methodology and inputs are correct and up-to-date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing monitoring of contract funding and costs by headquarters
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial annual contract award cost of an A-76 contract is used as the base for Coast Guard Headquarters funding of these contracts. After the initial funding was provided, the funding bases of these contracts have not changed. Also, contract costs have not been reviewed by HQ to see if costs have increased or decreased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement processes at HQ to periodically review and adjust funding bases in response to actual contract cost changes, deobligations, and wage adjustments so appropriations reflect current costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of recompete/award and contract extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract extensions are the rule for most of these contracts. In four out of the five cases, contract awards have been made from 1.5 months to one year after the end of the contract’s final option year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor procurement timelines to minimize gaps and extensions; identify bottlenecks (spec review, negotiations, DCAA audit lead time, heavy workload) and allocate resources to reduce award delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence and completeness of contractor QA Plan and Government QA Surveillance Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: A major problem is the lack of Quality Assurance (QA) Plan by the contractor, and the lack of a QA surveillance plan by the Government. These plans are essential to successfully monitor and administer the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require timely submission of contractor QA Plans and development of Government QA Surveillance Plans; use these to justify performance deductions and to guide routine surveillance activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor personnel qualifications and compliance with specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Early in the contract performance period, the contractor was unable to obtain fully qualified personnel and turnover was unusually high. Many of the new employees were hired off the street and were at times given a uniform and told to learn their tasks on the job. This was in violation with the contract specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify contractor hiring practices against specified qualification requirements; use hiring records, training logs, and surveillance to confirm compliance and take timely corrective action for violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PM leadership and communication skills as performance factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the Coast Guard contract specialist and COTR believe that the lack of leadership and poor communication skills exhibited by the contractor’s PM was a contributing factor to the contractor’s marginal performance on this contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate PM leadership and communication in performance reviews; where deficiencies exist, document impacts and require corrective measures or personnel changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation to justify performance deductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Without the QA Surveillance plan, it was difficult to properly justify the amount of these deductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain surveillance records, incident reports, and QA documentation to substantiate any monetary deductions for unsatisfactory performance; absence of documentation weakens enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and allocation of training responsibilities (legal/policy constraints)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an unresolved legal and policy issue which questions whether the Coast Guard can provide firearms training to non-Government civilians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify and document which party is responsible for specific training (contractor vs Government) and resolve any legal/policy constraints before performance begins to avoid training gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper MEO computation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: MEO costs were computed using instructions from the OMB Circular, which include using current standard Government GS and Military pay scales with annual inflation and retirement factors provided by OMB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow OMB Circular guidance when computing MEO costs, including pay scales, inflation, and retirement factors; ensure MEOs are recomputed when contract scope changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of original contract award value as basis for HQ funding
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of the original contract is used as a basis for allocation of funds by Coast Guard Headquarters for A-76 contracts, however funding levels are not monitored and do not change as contract costs increase or decrease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sole reliance on original award value for long-term funding; implement monitoring and adjustment mechanisms at HQ to reflect cost changes over the contract life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview/perception evaluation dimensions (six-question framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Six questions were used to gauge perceptions: (1) Is this commercial activity best conducted by military/Govt civilian/civilian contractor? (2) Are the specifications and contractor performance adequate? (3) Does the command have adequate control over the contracted-out activity? (4) What is the command’s overall relationship with the civilian contractor? (5) Do you believe that A-76 is a good process/idea? (6) Does the MEO need more personnel?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these six standardized questions to collect consistent perceptions from COs/XOs; record both categorical responses and supporting comments for context and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification flexibility vs rigidity
rubrics_metrics.description: The specifications are too rigid. Can’t anticipate changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether specifications are overly rigid and prevent adaptive responses; consider incorporating mechanisms to accommodate reasonable changes without undermining competition or control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of command control and responsiveness over contracted activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Are responses and remedies to problems timely? (Are responses and remedies to problems timely?)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the command’s ability to control contractor performance (response times, remedy effectiveness); consider administrative layers and time lags when evaluating adequacy of control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Root-cause identification for cost increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost increases were caused by wage and food price increases and in three cases, work was added to the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When costs rise, analyze root causes (wage determinations, commodity price inflation, added scope) and document adjustments, deobligations, or negotiations used to address them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and management of deobligations to offset food service cost changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost increases in food service contracts were offset by end of the fiscal year deobligations. Deobligations are made when the number of meals sold are below the original contract estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track meal volumes and use deobligations appropriately to reconcile actual consumption versus estimated obligations; ensure transparency and timeliness in deobligation accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need to recompute MEO after contract scope or performance changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The MEO for Support Center Seattle’s security contract does not reflect the current contract conditions and Government savings may not be accurately determined. The MEO needs to be recomputed because the original contract experienced a reduction in scope and significant drop in contract price in the second option year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recompute MEOs whenever contract scope or significant performance conditions change to ensure 'should cost' comparisons remain valid for oversight and recompete decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of award decision validity relative to MEO thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Using ... OMB Circular A-76 cost comparison guidelines, it appears that the original and second contract should not have been awarded. Even though the original contract’s actual cost of performance was 14.3 percent less than the MEO’s personnel cost, the original contract price was only 5.4 percent less than the MEO’s personnel cost instead of the required 10 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing award validity, compare both actual performance and original contract price to MEO thresholds; a contract should meet specified savings (e.g., 10%) at award decision time, not just in retrospective actuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of administrative workload and audit lead times on procurement schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: The delays in contract award have been attributed to slow specification review and approvals, long preparation time for negotiations, long DCAA audit lead time, and a heavy contract specialist workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor administrative cycle times (spec review, negotiations, DCAA audit) and adjust staffing or processes to reduce award delays; identify bottlenecks and implement corrective actions.
